newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to VSZ push Slovak SAX to 1997 year high.
newsitem.headline: Gains to VSZ push Slovak SAX to 1997 year high.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mostly higher in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with gains to steel producer VSZ pushing the SAX index to a year-high of 208.64 points.
VSZ traded 350,000 shares directly at 740 crowns, five crowns higher than the closing price on the BSE floor. Brokers said the deal in VSZ was expected to end a two month up-trend in the share.

"I think VSZ will ease, as this block was the main factor helping to keep the share price surprisingly high in recent weeks," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said, adding that the block was sold by a domestic shareholder to a foreign buyer.
VUB Kupon traded slightly less than 2.5 million shares in several tranches, at prices ranging from 565 to 780. The fund closed at 640 on the bourse floor.
Sykora said he expected the fund to decline, but other brokers were less sceptical.
"The long-standing battle between two investing groups in VUB Kupon now seems to be over, but the share can still be interesting," Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt said.
Overall, volume rose to 3,191,891 shares from 895,453 traded on Thursday, while turnover climbed to 2.39 billion crowns from 184.25 million.
